parsed.explanation: Adult alone: local facilities/services protected; border/federal facilities/custody remain high-risk. Travel docs mismatch can cause secondary, refusal, permanent bar. If detained, abuse/care denial severe. Adult with minor: state care/marker protections help, but federal anti-youth policies, funding pressure, and institutions complying with federal sports restrictions create care/school uncertainty. Protective state raises score above parent average but does not override federal gate; overall Elevated risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal rules require assigned-sex M/F passports/visas; X blocked for new issues; discrepancies may trigger secondary, evidence demands, refusal, or permanent fraud ineligibility. Travelers report passports blocked/confiscated; airport screening can out presentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; litigation challenges the marker policy; legal-aid FAQ exists. State marker self-ID and nonbinary IDs are resident-facing and do not cure foreign passport/visa mismatch.
entry_documents.interaction: Border/transit checkpoints are federal; every arrival can test documents, so state public-accommodation law cannot neutralize entry screening or marker mismatch.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If detained, federal immigration custody is documented severe: forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse justified by gender; federal corrections adopt conversion-therapy-like inmate rules and deny hormone care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division criminalizes neither bathroom use nor trans presentation; state hate-crime/civil-rights law apply to state custody, but no shield from federal immigration/corrections operations documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy can become investigation, removal or federal custody; at that stage birth-sex placement and abuse risk dominate state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive bars gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; airports and federal buildings apply birth-sex rules. Some parent states criminalise facilities, but the division itself does not.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division law protects public accommodations and has no facility restriction; its highest court upheld bathroom use aligned with gender identity; hate-crime and anti-panic repeal apply.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State/private facilities in the division are materially safer; federal and federally funded facilities remain universal exposure for any outed traveller.

care_services.exposure: Federal funding freezes, proposed youth reimbursement bars, hospital subpoenas and custody medication denial threaten care; ward placement in federal/federally funded facilities is uncertain.
care_services.protection: Division expressly protects gender-affirming care, allows 16-17 hormone therapy, no provider ban documented, and mandates SOGI data in healthcare facilities.
care_services.interaction: Routine care in the division can follow identity; public insurance, emergency settings or federal facilities may override under national rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders define sex by birth, remove gender-identity protections, direct law enforcement at schools, and use counterterrorism language around radical gender ideology/pro-trans groups; poll shows majorities support binary-document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division hate-crime enhancements, civil-rights enforcement, court-backed facilities and a low-risk national assessment are documented; local enforcement against facilities targeting is not documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing can license border/federal officers and chill providers/schools; local protections may resist, but enforcement statistics are absent.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal anti-minor care rhetoric, reimbursement rules, school/teacher investigations and funding threats can affect trans minors or guardians, especially in federally funded institutions or emergency care.
minors_guardians.protection: Division protects minors: marker self-ID with provider/parent consent, 16-17 hormone therapy, gender-affirming care safeguards and public accommodations law.
minors_guardians.interaction: State law is protective locally, but university/funding capitulations and federal immigration screening can still expose a travelling family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific violence figures or enforcement statistics; national hostility and other-state facility arrests may license local harassment, but no documented visitor targeting here.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division anti-discrimination, hate-crime enhancements, gay/trans panic ban and retained referendum protections support police and civil-remedy paths, though actual enforcement is undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local street incidents are likely protected; federal/transit incidents follow national posture, so jurisdiction of encounter determines exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions remain: airport/federal facility enforcement, hospital ward placement, detention placement, whether state remedies work for short visitors, and how injunctions affect current national rules.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State human-rights process, courts, advocacy FAQ and active litigation may help locally; federal immigration remedies are discretionary, slow or undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Combined remedies are split: local remedies can operate, but federal entry/custody exposure lacks an equally visible, prompt shield.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia criminalizes presentation and routinely holds visitors for months with beatings and capital threat. This division lacks local criminalization and protects care/facilities, so it is much safer; but federal entry/fraud screening and abusive immigration custody still keep it far below low-risk jurisdictions.

Similar in that identity mismatch creates routine checkpoint exposure and humiliation/denial of some services; this jurisdiction is safer locally because public-accommodation/care law and no facility ban operate, but federal border/facility/custody exposure prevents a materially higher score.

Higher than here: matching-marker passports, trained border officers, legal remedies and brief detention. This parent allows only assigned-sex M/F travel documents, possible visa refusals/permanent bars, and federal facilities/custody risks, so it is clearly less safe than 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is hostile federal plus protective division. Federal entry screening and assigned-sex documents create universal border exposure; if escalated, immigration/federal custody is severely abusive. State protections materially improve everyday local exposure: no facility ban, public accommodations/hate-crime, court-backed bathroom use, and care protections. They cannot cancel federal facilities, border, or immigration authority, and federal anti-minor/counterterrorism rhetoric chills services and institutions. Adult alone faces elevated risk; minor/guardian faces similar plus care/document/funding interaction. Remedies exist locally but are uneven at federal stage, so score sits in Elevated band.
